title: Everest Base Camp & Kala Patthar Trek
card_points: Everest Base Camp (5,486 m) & Kala Patthar
overview: A classic trek through the Khumbu to Everest Base Camp and the summit of Kala Patthar — passing through rhododendron forests, Sherpa villages and high glacial terrain, with views of Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse and Ama Dablam.

The itinerary includes two acclimatisation days, a visit to Tengboche Monastery and a sunrise climb of Kala Patthar. Experienced guides, porters, meals on the trek and high-altitude insurance are included. The itinerary is indicative and may change with weather and trail conditions.

highlights.title: Tengboche

highlights.title: Namche Bazaar

activities.title: Drive to Ramechhap
activities.text: For the early flight to Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly to Lukla (2,800 m) → Trek to Phakding (2,610 m)
itinerary.subtitle: 3–4 hours trekking

activities.title: Trek to Phakding
activities.text: A gentle first walk along the Dudh Kosi.

activities.title: Trek along the Dudh Kosi
activities.text: Cross two suspension bridges, then a steep two-hour climb to Namche.

activities.title: Trek to Tengboche
activities.text: Visit the monastery and attend a prayer ceremony, then continue to Deboche.

itinerary.title: Lobuche → Everest Base Camp (5,486 m) → Gorakshep (5,140 m)
itinerary.subtitle: 7–8 hours trekking

activities.title: Everest Base Camp
activities.text: Photos at base camp beside the Khumbu Icefall, then return to Gorakshep.

activities.title: Return & descend
activities.text: Back to Gorakshep for breakfast, then descend to Pheriche.

activities.title: Weather backup or leisure
activities.text: Half-day sightseeing if the buffer is not needed.

inclusions: Transfer to Ramechhap & domestic flights to Lukla
All meals on the trek, boiled water & hot drinks
First aid, emergency oxygen & communication devices
exclusions: Costs from weather changes or unforeseen events
Nepal visa fees for non-Indian passport holders

good_to_know.title: Fitness
good_to_know.text: Good cardiovascular fitness is essential. Start a training plan of walking, stair climbs and cardio at least 8–12 weeks before departure.

good_to_know.title: Gear
good_to_know.text: A detailed gear list is shared on booking. Personal trekking and mountaineering gear can be rented on request.

good_to_know.title: Altitude
good_to_know.text: The itinerary includes acclimatisation days. Guides monitor every trekker and the plan may change for safety.

good_to_know.title: Documents
good_to_know.text: A valid passport, visa where required, and medical and evacuation insurance details are needed before travel.

faqs.question: Where does the expedition start and end?
faqs.answer: The trek starts and ends in Kathmandu, with flights from Hyderabad included.

faqs.question: Do I need prior trekking experience?
faqs.answer: Prior multi-day trekking experience is recommended. Our team will talk you through fitness preparation before you book.

faqs.question: What happens if the weather turns?
faqs.answer: Buffer and reserve days are built in. Final decisions on summit attempts are made by the expedition leaders for everyone’s safety.

faqs.question: Who leads the expedition?
faqs.answer: Adventure journeys are run with Anmish Adventures, led by mountaineer Anmish Varma, with experienced local guides and support staff.
